head: kong
rule: กอง piles things up (1), and what is piled is either STUFF (2) or MEN (4). Sense 2 takes every mass gathered for a purpose and the abstractions built on one — the ritual fire (กองกูณฑ์), the ashes after a cremation (กองฟอน), an estate (กองมรดก), a fund (กองทุน), the common pool (กองกลาง). Sense 4 takes every organised body of personnel, and the RID's own เป็นต้น in that gloss is what lets the football lines in beside the armies: กองหน้า and กองหลัง are named the way กองหนุน and กองโจร are, a body of men with a station. Sense 1, the verb, takes the verb-on-verb compound ก่ายกอง, stacked-and-heaped, meaning abundantly. The classifier senses 3, 7 and 8 take no compounds — a classifier is used, not compounded — and 9 (the รกฟ้า tree) and 10 (the เป็นกอง intensifier, which the gloss ties to that one collocation) take nothing here either.
